correctness.rationale: For s≠0 the bijection w=2t/s−1 changes the ordinate to (w⁴+6w²+1)/8 after dividing by s⁴. Squaring w gives the involution v↦−6−v with a fixed point −3 and exceptional pair {0,−6}; their distinct targets have multiplicities 1+δ and 2+η. The character-product sum is −ε: after shifting v by 3 and taking out χ(−1), the sum of χ(z²−9) is −1 by counting (z-u)(z+u)=9. Removing the three exceptional points gives precisely the three orbit equations and their solutions. Half of the nonzero discriminants are nonsquares, and including their targets gives the asserted k₀. At s=0 the fourth-power map on F× has kernel size g, including the separate singleton at y=0. Aggregation, 8/g=3−ε, and summation of squared multiplicities give the stated global spectrum, support and (known) energy. Independent direct ordered enumeration checks each slice, including zeros, over q=5,7,11,13,19,29,49,125, with an irreducible cubic model for F₁₂₅; all counts, support and energy agree.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration is only corroboration. The character argument proves the characteristic >3 result, including nonprime fields, but says nothing about characteristics two and three.

evidence: The 2024 text explicitly credits the odd-characteristic Dickson value-set formula to Theorem 10 of the 1988 paper. Using the source's body notation d=gcd(4,q−1), e=gcd(4,q+1), its specialization gives S=floor((q−1)/(2d))+floor((q+1)/(2e))+1+1_{η=−1, q≡3 or 5 mod 8}. The prefatory Theorem 1.4 has a garbled gcd and power-of-two specification; the specialization is checked against the actual image decomposition, not that typo. In §2 and §3 write D₄ as z+a⁴/z on z from the fourth powers of F_q× and of the norm-a coset. These power sets have sizes (q−1)/d and (q+1)/e, with z↔a⁴/z giving distinct pairs except at ±a². The two images can overlap only at these two fixed points; their symmetric-difference count on the two power sets is one for q≡1,7 mod 8 and is zero for η=1 or two for η=−1 when q≡3,5 mod 8. This gives the stated floor formula. The 2026/11/2 catalogue theorem also covers the complete histogram exactly at perturbation parameter zero, but postdates the frozen record.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Using χ(2)=1 for q≡1,7 mod 8 and −1 for q≡3,5 mod 8, and δ=ηχ(2), the floor formula is precisely S=(3q+4+ε+2δ−2η)/8 for every field in scope. This is not an implication from the later catalogue theorem alone.

evidence: Let S be the known nonzero-s image size. Parity under w↦−w puts the only odd-sized fiber at the target of w=0, where w²(w²+6)=0 has L=2+η roots. All other positive fibers are of size two or four since the polynomial is even and degree four. Thus k₂+k₄=S−1 and 2k₂+4k₄=q−L; k₀=q−S and the odd counts are forced by L.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Solving those two elementary equations reproduces k₂ and k₄, and adding the fourth-power zero-slice gives all N_j and the sumset size. Thus the strongest prior implication uses the image theorem, not the earlier energy identity. No distinct nonmechanical remainder is established.

evidence: For s≠0 the frozen ordinate is an affine transform of D₄(w,a)=w⁴−4aw²+2a² for a=−3/2. In particular χ(a)=η. The 2024 paper gives the first-kind recurrence/Binet formula, the hyperbolic and elliptic images and their overlap, and states the size of the value set over arbitrary odd prime powers.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The nonzero-s slice is literally the image of a known Dickson polynomial after bijective changes of source and target. No new count of such images is needed. At s=0 the support is the standard cyclic-group fourth-power image plus zero.

originality.rationale: An older, broader Dickson-polynomial value-set theorem supplies the entire claimed support calculation. Taking its degree-four case and using one exceptional fiber plus total mass then mechanically recovers the whole claimed multiplicity histogram, not only its second moment. This is established by a statement-level specialization of pre-2026 literature, not by the inability to retrieve other papers or the date of a later catalogue record.
residual_risks: No claim that the earlier sources literally tabulate the graph histogram; it is mechanically implied by an earlier uniform image formula. The exact scope of the 2016 article beyond its indexed abstract and the cited finite tables remain unverified; neither is needed for the decision.

value.rationale: The ordered convolution histogram is a natural invariant, and the direct quadratic-character proof is readable. But for this exact classification the old Dickson value-set theorem plus parity and total mass already determines every entry. Recasting that consequence in graph notation and adding the cyclic-group zero slice does not supply a distinct exact invariant under the value criterion. A useful exposition is not a repaired new finding.
residual_risks: No decision is made on the novelty or value of a different weighted problem or a larger quartic family. No surviving new statement warranted a repair of this record.
